subject: Post-demo: EdgeStream live-probe scripting handoff & streaming SLO checklist
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rios <tom.rios@edgestream.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: live-probe scripting handoff & streaming SLO checklist

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great to see the streaming pipelines in action. Per our call, I wanted to capture the concrete next steps so we can get your customer-led load run scheduled and make sure the SLOs we validated in the demo translate to the load window.

Summary of requirements we discussed (please confirm):
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end event-to-response < 300ms for non-batched streaming calls; p99 < 600ms in peak microbursts.
- Throughput: sustained 1,200 req/s for ingest tier during the 2-hour window; peak bursts up to 2,500 req/s.
- Concurrency: ~250 concurrent streaming sessions with KV-cache reuse expected.
- Streaming chunking: clients will send events in 256-token windows; Redwood should maintain per-session KV cache for duration of session (~5–10 min).
- Test tooling: customer will drive k6 probes (we also have a Locust fallback). You mentioned sharing a k6 package and test accounts.

What Redwood will provide before the run:
1) Test accounts (API keys scoped to sandbox) and per-test target hostnames.
2) IP allowlist entries for the test runner and expected ranges.
3) Baseline profile of observed p50/p95/p99 from the demo environment and expected token billing estimates.
4) A short runbook (15–20 minute playbook) for failover and rollback if SLOs are violated.

Can you confirm the test window you prefer and attach the k6 bundle you mentioned? Once we have the script I’ll loop in Ben to provision the creds and whitelists.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: streaming_slo_profile_v1.csv (summary of demo traces)

From: Tom Rios <tom.rios@edgestream.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha@edgestream.ai>, qa@edgestream.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 17:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: live-probe scripting handoff & streaming SLO checklist

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the summary — looks good and captures the ask. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 2-hour window on Wed 2028-02-21 10:00–12:00 PT works for our ops and QA teams.
- k6 bundle is attached (edgestream_k6_v2.tar.gz) and the test contains three phases: ramp (20m), steady (80m), spike-burst (20m).
- We’ll use the following origin IPs for the run: 198.51.100.0/24 (primary runners) and 203.0.113.0/28 (burst runners). Please add both to your allowlist.
- Test accounts: we need two sandbox API keys and one admin-level key for live monitoring.

Notes on the script: it performs continuous streaming connections that send 256-token batches and expects incremental chunked responses. The built-in assertions check p95 < 320ms (we set slightly looser to validate). We’d like Redwood to run a short smoke run with 50 concurrent sessions before the main window so we can sanity-check connectivity.

Let me know when the API keys and allowlist are ready and if you can provide an external endpoint for TLS fingerprinting.

—Tom
Tom Rios
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeStream Analytics
tom.rios@edgestream.ai

Attachment: edgestream_k6_v2.tar.gz

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Tom Rios <tom.rios@edgestream.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: live-probe scripting handoff & streaming SLO checklist

Tom / Naomi —

I’ve provisioned the sandbox keys and created a short-lived admin key for the run. Keys have been uploaded to the shared Drive folder and I pasted them into a secured HubSpot note (HS-4128).

Allowlist entries I added to our perimeter rules:
- 198.51.100.0/24 (k6 primary)
- 203.0.113.0/28 (burst runners)

If you need additional CIDR ranges, tell me and I’ll expand. For TLS fingerprinting, we can provide an endpoint at https://sandbox-api.redwood.ai/edgestream-probe (valid cert, mutual TLS not required for this run).

Smoke run plan: Naomi — I propose we run the 50-session smoke on Tue 2028-02-21 09:15–09:30 PT (45 minutes before your main window) so EdgeStream can validate client-side behavior and Redwood can confirm KV cache warming. Ben and I will be on the call for monitoring.

I’m attaching a tiny README in Drive with the key locations and the dashboard links.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Related Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-EdgeStream-TestAssets, HubSpot:HS-4128

From: Tom Rios <tom.rios@edgestream.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha@edgestream.ai>, qa@edgestream.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Feb 2028 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: live-probe scripting handoff & streaming SLO checklist

Ben / Naomi —

All set on our side — smoke run complete (50 sessions) and the k6 checks passed. We’ll begin the steady window now (10:00 PT). Dashboard looks healthy; we’ll report immediately if p95 drifts over 320ms.

Thanks for the quick turnaround on keys and allowlist. I’ll file a short post-run summary after the window.

Tom
Tom Rios
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeStream Analytics
